# Preface {.unnumbered}

This textbook accompanies the lecture **Supply Chain Management (SCM)** and expands on the content of the lecture slides (`slides/`) in detailed, text-based form. It is intended as a **course reader for self-study**: while the slides serve as a visual aid to memory in the lecture, this book explains the same models, methods and case examples in full sentences, with derived formulas and runnable, commented R code.

**This course reader is primarily AI-generated and requires further correction. Any errors can be reported to thomas.kirschstein@hs-rm.de.**

## Structure of the book

The chapters follow the lecture units, which are divided into three blocks: **fundamentals of supply chain management**, **strategic design of supply chains** and **uncertainty and risk management in supply chains**.

1. **Introduction and basic concepts of supply chain management** — What is a supply chain? Flows, actors, structures, supply chain profit and double marginalisation.
2. **Value creation, strategic manufacturing and strategic fit** — Value creation process, decoupling point, make-or-buy, implied uncertainty, strategic fit.
3. **Objectives, trade-offs and logistics costs** — The SCM system of objectives, the tetrahedron of trade-offs, cost types and the introduction of the case study **SushiFresh GmbH**.
4. **Sustainability in supply chain management** — In-depth treatment of the sustainability content from unit 3: environmental strategic fit, environmental SCM strategies, circular economy and circular supply chains.
5. **Facility location planning I** — Qualitative methods (scoring model, AHP) and continuous methods (centre-of-gravity method, Weiszfeld algorithm).
6. **Facility location planning II** — Discrete network planning models: transportation problem, warehouse location problem, heuristics and exact methods.
7. **Uncertainty in supply chains and pooling** — Demand uncertainty, capacity and inventory pooling, safety stocks, the square-root law of risk pooling.
8. **The newsvendor model** — Optimal order quantities under uncertainty, critical ratio, service level.
9. **The bullwhip effect and the Beer Game** — Amplification of demand fluctuations along the chain, causes and countermeasures.

From Chapter [-@sec-logistikkosten] onwards, a continuous case example accompanies the course reader: the fictitious **SushiFresh GmbH** produces fresh sushi boxes for supermarkets in the Rhine-Main area. As in the lecture, it is used to work through location choice, network design, safety stocks, production quantities and the bullwhip effect.

Each chapter follows the same structure:

- **Learning objectives** at the beginning, so that it is clear which competences are to be acquired.
- **Conceptual explanations** with examples from practice.
- **In-depth theory boxes** (shaded purple), which present theoretical background, derivations and links to the academic literature in more detail than the slides.
- **Case study boxes** (shaded yellow) on SushiFresh GmbH.
- **Mathematical derivations** in easy-to-follow steps.
- **Commented R code** that calculates and visualises the models directly — every code block is runnable and commented so that even students with no prior experience of R can follow the process. Alongside the subject content, basic R concepts (vectors, functions, data frames, the `tidyverse`, pipes `|>`, visualisation with `ggplot2`) are introduced step by step.
- **Review questions** at the end of each chapter for self-assessment.

## Prerequisites

- Fundamentals of linear algebra and probability theory.
- No prior knowledge of R required — the basics are introduced in the book.
- Fundamentals of microeconomics are helpful but not essential.

## Software

All R code in this book uses the following packages:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse",       # data manipulation (dplyr, tidyr) and visualisation (ggplot2)
  "plotly",          # interactive graphics
  "knitr",           # embedding R code in Quarto documents
  "kableExtra",      # formatted tables
  "sf",              # processing geodata
  "leaflet",         # interactive maps
  "ompr", "ompr.roi", "ROI.plugin.glpk",  # algebraic optimisation models (MILP)
  "scales"           # axis and number formatting in ggplot2
))
```

All example functions (e.g. for the centre-of-gravity method, the newsvendor model or the add/drop heuristic) are also bundled in `R/scm_functions.R` and are referenced at the appropriate points in the book.

## Recommended reading

The main textbook is:

> Chopra, S., & Meindl, P. *Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation*. Pearson.

In addition, the text draws on, among others: Thonemann, Günther & Tempelmeier  as well as Cachon & Terwich (for full details see [References](references.qmd)).
